finalAnswer:
Created **[CareLink platform architecture](<temp>\project\.archi-made-easy\architecture-carelink-20261110-235500\carelink-architecture.html)** — one Azure EU region across three zones, with the clinics' FHIR system kept as the system of record.

The shape of the answer: patients and clinicians enter through Front Door + API Management into a Booking API and a Consultation API; everything slow or failure-prone leaves the request path through Service Bus (reminders, note write-back, prescriptions, audit events), and the two bought services stay out of the data path entirely — video media and card details never traverse the platform, which is also why 25 concurrent consultations per clinic cost you no compute.

**Assumptions I made**
- One region with three availability zones, not a second region (open question 2) — recorded as a *proposed* decision with the alternative costed out, not settled.
- No consultation recordings (open question 1), so no media storage is drawn.
- Two identity tenants: workforce Entra ID for clinicians, staff and admins; Entra External ID for patients, with the verification provider called from sign-up.
- Timeouts, retries, autoscale ranges and the call ratios between tiers are design intent — no latency, traffic mix or cost figures were invented, so the cost model holds only your EUR 30,000 budget (recorded as 30,000 currency units, excluding the video and payment providers).
- The EU region itself is not chosen.

**Two things the model flags, from running review on the declared design**
- The 1-hour recovery time cannot cover a whole-region outage with a single region. Either that objective is understood as in-region only (zone loss, data corruption → point-in-time restore), or the second region needs funding. This is the real content of open question 2.
- The modelled critical path P99 is 1,530 ms, but it runs through the one-time sign-up identity check (patient → Entra External ID → verification provider), which your 800 ms target for *search and booking* doesn't cover. Worth confirming that scope in writing.

**Not represented**: search facets (speciality, language, availability) live inside the Booking API rather than as components; CI/CD, environments, observability and private networking are outside the requirements document; and the clinics' on-premises system has no stated recovery objectives — that's an open item to put to them, since your records RPO/RTO depends on it.

Open the page and use the **Workbench** button with the mode rail on the left (Review, Simulate, Optimize) to try zone or provider failures, the Monday-morning surge, and the second-region alternative yourself. Those results are an analytical model of this design, not measurements. Automated checks passed; I have not visually reviewed the rendering.
